items: xAI describes Grok 4.7's longer-horizon training and reports multi-hour task results — importance 5/10 · In a September 21 release, xAI described Grok 4.7 as using a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour tasks, and training to understand the Grok Bot harness. The release reports Grok 4.7 scores across coding, office, terminal, legal, electrical-engineering and clinical benchmarks, including 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6. These are company-reported results; the page does not provide test protocols, sample sizes or uncertainty. — FCMO-3B81F3E90D86

Marvell announces 2nm 400G-per-lane optical demonstrations aimed at 3.2T AI data-center links — importance 4/10 · In a September 21, 2026 announcement for ECOC, Marvell said it planned to demonstrate 2nm 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 and described it as enabling a transition toward 3.2T data-center connectivity. The company also announced planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec and 1.6T ZR/coherent-lite demonstrations. The source establishes the company’s announcement and intended showcase, not independent observation of the demos or measured product performance. It provides no lane power, optical reach, error rate, qualification status or production schedule for the 400G/lane technology. — FCMO-A4319B48FABA

Constrained binary optimization selects non-consecutive transformer blocks for depth pruning — importance 5/10 · A September 11 revision of a preprint formulates transformer-block removal as a constrained binary optimization problem. It uses second-order interactions among binary keep/remove variables, derived from calibration-set gradients, to rank block combinations; several low-energy configurations may be worth testing because the lowest-energy one is not always best downstream. Without retraining, the authors report that removing 40 of 80 Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct blocks yields 76.9 MMLU for their method versus 54.0 for block influence, a 22.9-point difference, with better scores across the listed benchmarks. They also report results on a heterogeneous Nemotron MoE model without retraining. Results are author-reported and benchmark-specific; calibration data matters, candidate selection is manual, and the best pruning method varies by task. — FCMO-1A008E4E6967

An open FlashAttention mapping on AMD XDNA 2 moves long-sequence attention into the compute-bound regime — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint compares four FlashAttention mappings on AMD XDNA 1 and XDNA 2 accelerators. On a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with XDNA 2, its fused MLIR-AIR mapping keeps attention-score intermediates in compute-tile memory and uses the cascade interconnect for reductions; for GPT-2 Small dimensions it reports 3.62 effective GEMM TFLOP/s at 32K sequence length, about 2.0× the IRON mapping. The authors also report 6.5× energy efficiency over an optimized Triton/ROCm integrated-GPU implementation on the same system at 32K. This is a paper-reported operator result, not end-to-end LLM serving or independently reproduced deployment performance. — FCMO-9EAC166A2708

MAAP turns cooperating robot arms into active perception viewpoints; role-conditioned control improves selected tasks — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint presents Multi-Agent Active Perception (MAAP), which uses wrist cameras already carried by collaborating robot arms as moving viewpoints, and Role-Aware Imitation Learning (RAIL), which predicts each arm’s manipulation or perception role and conditions its actions on that role. Across four simulated tasks, the authors report mean success rising from 56.5% with a fixed global view to 70.0% with all wrist views and 79.2% with RAIL on the same multi-view inputs. On one dual-arm real-robot placement task, the combined system succeeds in 14 of 20 trials versus 0 of 20 for fixed-view ACT, but that hardware comparison changes both visual input and controller. Results are single-training-run paper claims and do not compare against a dedicated sensing arm. — FCMO-B9E97B1EC418

Differentiable soft-symbolic planning links visual uncertainty to rule-constrained action planning — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint presents a differentiable planner that keeps visual scene relations as continuous symbolic beliefs, propagates actions through soft logical transition rules, and lets the task objective update both action choices and perception parameters. On Blocksworld, the authors report 40/40 valid solutions on LatPlan-40 versus 33/40 for LatPlan and 596/600 on PlanBench-600 versus the published o1-preview score of 587/600. On a fixed 100-instance blurred-image subset, planning gradients raise valid plans from 59/100 with frozen perception to 83/100. The approach also reports results on Logistics and Sokoban. These are paper-reported, domain-specific results; solve-time and estimated-cost comparisons use different systems and are not a matched economic comparison. — FCMO-741AF584E339
